name: Wendy Bauer

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I am from the independent Work Futures Panel, and what you say here is confidential. What is an ordinary workday like for you?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I am 43 and lead the final review of accounts and tax returns, usually with a pile of client folders by nine. I like showing a junior how a handwritten receipt changes a figure, and I dislike the rush to sign a return before anyone can explain it. I have a master’s degree and a chartered accountancy qualification, but I have never used AI tools at work; I prefer to see the source paper first.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. "Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway."

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In that picture, I would still be at my desk with a folder of receipts and a return to sign. A little software help would not change who answers a client question.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the team to leave the source papers attached to each account. I can explain a correction better when I can show the client the exact receipt.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I do not use AI tools and I am slow to trust a new screen, even though colleagues use them. My senior pay and our ten months of savings are comfortable, but the mortgage and two school children still make mistakes expensive.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep preparing and signing the firm tax returns I am assigned, and ask my manager Lydia to protect a paper source check in the review checklist. I would mark any repeat errors in the client folder rather than trying an AI tool on live records.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel calm about my own job in a mild change. Plenty of firms nearby still need chartered accountants, and we have room to handle a rough month.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Can you recall a client record that mattered?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A cafe client once brought a handwritten till sheet that corrected an electronic total. I could point to the sheet when she asked why her tax figure moved.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Who would change the checklist?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Lydia runs our review meetings, so I would bring the cafe folder there and ask for a source check in the checklist. If she says no, my own assigned returns still get checked before I sign.

say: I would keep **source papers** attached to every account I sign.
I would show colleagues the **cafe till sheet** that corrected an electronic total.
think: I have never used **AI tools** on client records, and a new screen earns trust slowly.
My **ten month reserve** is comfortable, though the mortgage and children still need income.
do: Keep preparing **assigned tax returns** and checking original receipts before signing.
Ask Lydia to retain a **paper source check** in the team review checklist.
feel: **Calm** about my role and household in this mild picture.
S0.quote: I can explain a correction better when I can show the client the exact receipt.
fieldNote: Wendy’s **cafe example** shows why she prefers a source sheet to a tidy electronic total when explaining a tax correction.
Her **high pay and savings** support a calm response; she sees plenty of nearby employers if ordinary work goes badly.

steps.text: Keep signing assigned returns after checking original client receipts
Bring cafe folder to Lydia’s review meeting and request paper checklist

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. "Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust."

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: That is a bigger change; writing and checking returns are most of our work. I would want Lydia to tell us which review jobs remain paid before a new system is introduced.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell clients that our firm should name the person responsible for any automated return. I would also ask for a clear way to challenge a wrong figure.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think my own review hours could shrink, despite seniority, because software can check more than a junior draft. I could probably find another accounting job nearby, but an advertised vacancy is different from a guess.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep assigned paid returns and ask Lydia for a manual exception route in the new review process. If my hours actually fall, I will apply to posted tax manager openings, leaving only after written pay, start date and hours cover the mortgage and school pickup.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about my hours, although ten months saved means we are not cornered. I do not want to use client data in an AI trial just to look willing.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would a manual exception look like?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: An exception would be a disputed invoice that a person checks against the original, with a named sign off. I would ask Lydia for that in writing before the software goes live.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would make you change firms?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would take a tax manager job if the pay and hours were real, not on a recruiter call alone. My partner Arun takes the children to school; I handle pickup, so late shifts would not work.

say: I would ask Lydia to name **paid review roles** before the new system goes live.
I would tell clients who is **responsible** for an automated return and how to challenge it.
think: My own **review hours** could shrink even with seniority.
Nearby jobs are plausible, but a **posted vacancy** and written terms have to exist.
do: Keep **assigned paid returns** and request a written manual exception route for disputed invoices.
If hours fall, seek **posted tax manager work** with written mortgage covering pay, start and pickup compatible hours.
feel: **Anxious** about my own hours, buffered by savings.
S1.quote: My partner Arun takes the children to school; I handle pickup, so late shifts would not work.
fieldNote: She prefers a **manual exception** with original invoices and named sign off to an unapproved experiment on client records.
Her potential **job change** depends on actual reduced hours, a posted opening and written terms compatible with pickup.

steps.text: Keep assigned paid returns and request written manual exception route
If hours fall, seek posted manager job with written mortgage covering pay, start and pickup hours

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. "Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare."

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Full AGI by 2028 would reach our desks first; I cannot wait for the 2031 robots to see what happens. I would ask Lydia for actual contract dates.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell clients the firm must say who signs their accounts during a machine transition. I would not promise that a human signature keeps every wage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect much of my paid review work to vanish in the first year after 2028, and I may be dismissed. Ten months saved buys breathing room, but our mortgage does not stop.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would cancel our second streaming and sports package this billing month and put that freed payment toward future bills. While the firm still assigns paid returns, I would finish them; after dismissal I would apply for posted payroll supervisor jobs only with written pay, start and hours fitting the mortgage and school pickup.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel alarmed because I expect my own salary to be hit. The savings let me make calls carefully, but they do not make job loss gentle.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which bill could you actually stop now?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The subscription cut is small, but it is a bill I can stop without changing the children’s school routine. Arun and I can review the bigger expenses only if the dismissal letter comes.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why seek payroll supervision?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I know payroll records and tax withholding, but I have not held a supervisor post in payroll. I would apply to real openings and show my chartered work, not describe myself as already hired.

say: I would seek **contract dates** because AGI reaches our accounts desk in 2028.
I would ask who **signs accounts** during the transition.
think: I expect my **paid review work** to vanish quickly after AGI.
Ten months saved helps, but the **mortgage** keeps coming.
do: Cancel the extra **sports subscription** this month and retain the freed payment for bills.
After dismissal, seek **posted payroll supervision** only with written mortgage covering pay, start and pickup compatible hours.
Finish **assigned paid returns** only while the firm still offers them before dismissal.
feel: **Alarmed** about likely salary loss despite savings.
S2.quote: Ten months saved buys breathing room, but our mortgage does not stop.
fieldNote: She cuts a named **subscription bill**, protecting school routine while reserving larger household changes for actual dismissal.
The **payroll move** relies on transferable records skills but remains a posted, written offer rather than a claimed job.

steps.text: Cancel extra sports and streaming package this billing month
Finish assigned paid returns only while firm offers them
After dismissal, seek posted payroll job with written mortgage covering pay, start and pickup hours

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. "Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast."

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Five years to 2031 is enough time to learn payroll supervision properly if someone will let me see the work. The 2034 robots are beside the point for returns and pay records.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell Lydia that staff need paid places to learn the payroll deadlines, not an instruction to watch a video at home. A real month end cycle would show me whether I could do the job.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I still expect standard tax returns to be under pressure when AGI reaches the desk. Our ten month reserve makes a careful learning move possible, but I would keep present wages while the firm still has work.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask Lydia for paid supervised time on one payroll month end with the payroll lead, Nina, and take that assignment if approved. If denied, I will work free published payroll examples at home while keeping current paid accounts; I would seek a posted payroll vacancy only with written pay covering our mortgage, a confirmed start and pickup hours fitting our household. In the first year after 2031, if paid accounts end before a suitable offer, I would use our reserve for bills while seeking that posted payroll work.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious but there is room to learn without risking a client deadline. I am not ready to call myself a payroll supervisor because I have read examples.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would one supervised cycle involve?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: One month end means checking a pay run against the source timesheets and meeting the filing date with Nina watching. I need one supervised payroll cycle, not just the screen layout.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What hours would make a vacancy workable?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Our younger child finishes school pickup at four, so a shift that runs to seven is not a workable offer. Arun can cover a rare late day, but not every week.

say: I would ask for a **paid payroll placement** with a real month end cycle.
I would explain that **2031 desk work** changes before the later robots matter.
think: Standard **tax returns** are still at risk even with five years.
Our **ten month reserve** allows careful learning while present wages last.
do: Complete one **supervised payroll cycle** only if Lydia assigns paid time with Nina; otherwise practise free examples.
Seek a **posted payroll role** only with written mortgage covering pay, start and pickup compatible hours.
Use the **reserve for bills** after 2031 if paid accounts end before a qualifying payroll offer.
feel: **Anxious** about future pay, with time for practical learning.
S3.quote: I need one supervised payroll cycle, not just the screen layout.
fieldNote: Her **one month end** is a real learning task involving timesheets, filing dates and payroll lead supervision.
If refused, she uses **free examples** and current paid accounts; an outside role still requires written household fitting terms.

steps.text: Complete payroll month end with Nina if Lydia assigns supervised paid time
Otherwise practise free examples while assigned paid accounts remain
Seek posted payroll role with written mortgage covering pay, start and pickup hours
Use reserve for bills after 2031 if paid accounts end before qualifying offer

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. "Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans."

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Ten years to 2036 takes our children through school, though the accounts desk still meets AGI in 2036 rather than the 2039 robot date. I can plan without guessing which firm will survive.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell colleagues to keep the paper evidence for every tax season we still handle. I would ask Lydia to tell us openly if the paid review rota starts shrinking.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I might still have high senior pay for years and then see our tax contracts fall after 2036. I have savings and local options, but the mortgage needs actual income, not a title.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep assigned paid returns and review our mortgage terms with Arun each autumn, without claiming a saving until the lender gives us an offer. If contracts shrink after 2036, I would apply for a posted payroll manager vacancy only with written pay, start and hours covering the mortgage and any school pickup needs that remain.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel uneasy now, with time and savings to make a careful choice. I would be anxious if the contracts actually fell.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you pay for payroll training yourself?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I do not want to pay for a speculative course out of the family reserve. If Lydia offers a funded paid supervised payroll cycle, I will take one; if not, I will keep practising on free examples while my present salary lasts.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you do with a mortgage rate offer?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Arun and I can ask the lender for a written rate offer in autumn, but we will not budget around a lower payment before we get one. That is how we keep the cushion real.

say: I would ask for **open review rotas** if paid work begins to shrink.
I would retain **paper evidence** for the accounts we still sign.
think: Senior pay may not survive **post 2036 contract loss**.
Our **mortgage** needs actual wages despite savings and nearby firms.
do: Keep **paid returns** while assigned and seek a written mortgage rate offer each autumn before changing the budget.
After 2036 cuts, seek **posted payroll management** with written mortgage covering pay, start and hours fitting any remaining school needs.
Take a **paid supervised payroll cycle** only if Lydia funds it; otherwise practise free examples while present salary lasts.
feel: **Uneasy** now, with future anxiety if contracts shrink.
S4.quote: I have savings and local options, but the mortgage needs actual income, not a title.
fieldNote: She will seek a **written lender offer** before treating a possible lower rate as new disposable income.
A **funded supervised cycle** remains possible, but the family reserve is not spent on speculative course fees.

steps.text: Keep assigned paid returns while offered and request written mortgage rate each autumn
Take supervised paid payroll cycle if Lydia funds; otherwise practise free examples
After 2036 cuts, seek posted payroll job with written mortgage covering pay, start and hours

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: The 2028 AGI picture worries me most, because I expect paid review hours to vanish while our mortgage stays. Honest contract dates and a real posted payroll role with written terms would help me plan.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You did not ask what I would keep on my desk. I would keep the cafe till sheet because it reminds me why a client needs an explanation, not a clean looking total.

headlineQuote: I would keep the cafe till sheet because it reminds me why a client needs an explanation, not a clean looking total.
portrait: Wendy is a **43 year old** senior accountant with a master’s degree and chartered qualification who teaches juniors from original records.
She earns **higher pay**, has ten months saved, a mortgage, a partner and two school children, with plenty of nearby firms.
She has **never used AI** at work and seeks manual exceptions before trusting a new review system.
She tries **supervised payroll practice** only with paid assignment, then requires posted written offers for any later move.
biggestWorry: The **2028 AGI** picture threatens her own paid review hours while the household mortgage remains.
whatWouldHelp: Honest **contract dates** and a posted payroll job with written household fitting terms would help.
